rows.source: DVSA HGV daily walkaround safety checks
rows.verified: An HGV driver is responsible for making sure the vehicle is safe to drive.

rows.source: DVSA HGV daily walkaround safety checks
rows.verified: A walkaround check should be carried out before the journey.

rows.source: DVSA HGV daily walkaround safety checks
rows.verified: Defects must be recorded and reported in writing to the responsible person.

rows.source: DVSA HGV daily walkaround safety checks
rows.verified: Checks cover the vehicle interior and exterior.

rows.source: DVSA HGV daily walkaround safety checks
rows.verified: Lights, tyres, wheels, brakes, steering, mirrors and body condition are among the safety-critical items.

rows.source: DVSA HGV daily walkaround safety checks
rows.verified: Loads, doors, couplings and securing equipment must be checked where applicable.

rows.source: DVSA HGV daily walkaround safety checks
rows.verified: Police and DVSA officers may stop vehicles for roadside checks.

rows.source: DVSA HGV daily walkaround safety checks
rows.verified: A vehicle can be prohibited from use until serious defects are corrected.

rows.source: DVSA HGV daily walkaround safety checks
rows.verified: HGV walkaround risk depends on vehicle configuration, load, defect condition, maintenance, route, weather and driver competence.

rows.source: DVSA HGV daily walkaround safety checks
rows.verified: HGV-check evidence is vehicle-, defect-, journey-, operator- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.

rows.source: DVSA heavy-vehicle brake-test best practice
rows.verified: Heavy vehicles should be properly prepared before the annual brake test.

rows.source: DVSA heavy-vehicle brake-test best practice
rows.verified: Brake testing equipment should be maintained and calibrated to manufacturer instructions.

rows.source: DVSA heavy-vehicle brake-test best practice
rows.verified: Roller brake-test surfaces should be clean, in good condition and adequately gritted.

rows.source: DVSA heavy-vehicle brake-test best practice
rows.verified: Vehicles should normally be presented loaded to at least 65% of design axle weight unless exempt.

rows.source: DVSA heavy-vehicle brake-test best practice
rows.verified: Operators should follow the DVSA brake-test procedure and inspection manual.

rows.source: DVSA heavy-vehicle brake-test best practice
rows.verified: Correct vehicle data are needed to calculate brake performance.

rows.source: DVSA heavy-vehicle brake-test best practice
rows.verified: Maintenance records and regular brake-performance assessment support roadworthiness.

rows.source: DVSA heavy-vehicle brake-test best practice
rows.verified: Defects identified during preparation should be repaired before the statutory test.

rows.source: DVSA heavy-vehicle brake-test best practice
rows.verified: Heavy-vehicle brake risk depends on system design, load, adjustment, wear, maintenance, test method and operating conditions.

rows.source: DVSA heavy-vehicle brake-test best practice
rows.verified: Brake-test evidence is vehicle-, axle-, load-, maintenance- and test-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.
